refnamediv.refpurpose: Attach a filter to a stream

refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.parameters;
stream
The target stream.
filter_name
The filter name.
mode
By default, stream_filter_append will attach the filter to the read filter chain if the file was opened for reading (i.e. File Mode: r, and/or +). The filter will also be attached to the write filter chain if the file was opened for writing (i.e. File Mode: w, a, and/or +). STREAM_FILTER_READ, STREAM_FILTER_WRITE, and/or STREAM_FILTER_ALL can also be passed to the mode parameter to override this behavior. Bits other than STREAM_FILTER_READ and STREAM_FILTER_WRITE are ignored.
A stream opened with the x or c mode (without +) matches none of the modes above: when mode is omitted, the function returns &false; without any diagnostic and attaches no filter.
params
The parameters passed as is to the filter: a user filter finds them in $this->params, whereas the built-in convert.* and zlib.* filters read an array. An explicit &null; is not the same as omitting the parameter: the convert.* filters then fail to be created.
This filter will be added with the specified params to the end of the list and will therefore be called last during stream operations. To add a filter to the beginning of the list, use stream_filter_prepend.

&reftitle.notes;
When using custom (user) filters
stream_filter_register must be called first in order to register the desired user filter to filter_name.
Stream data is read from resources (both local and remote) in chunks, with any unconsumed data kept in internal buffers. When a new filter is appended to a stream, data in the internal buffers is processed through the new filter at that time. This differs from the behavior of stream_filter_prepend.
When a filter is added for read and write, two instances of the filter are created. stream_filter_append must be called twice with STREAM_FILTER_READ and STREAM_FILTER_WRITE to get both filter resources.
A filter that keeps a state, such as convert.base64-encode, keeps it across fseek and rewind, so the data read or written afterwards is wrong. A stateless filter such as string.rot13 is not affected.
